doc.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020

title: Reading liner notes and spotting lead players
summary: Both men loved liner notes; Bergeron kept seeing Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley and Gary Grant, and Snooky Young on pop records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Speaking of being a kid, I recall, I was a reader of liner notes on LPs, right?

So you see, okay here’s Frank Wess with Basie and then you see Frank Wess over here. And here’s Snooky Young here, and then he shows up — and I used to just love watching the musical chairs. And I’m wondering if you were like that, and did you latch on to some of those lead trumpet players?

Most definitely. And more in the pop world, because I would look at all these records and I kept seeing these three names: Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley, and Gary Grant. I mean on every record that I liked, you know, whether it was an Earth, Wind and Fire record or whatever, I would just keep seeing these names. I go man who are these? They’re on everything. And everything they do sounds great too you know. And so when one of them wasn’t there, you know as a kid I’d look at those things and go, “Wow, Chuck Findley’s not on this one. And Steve Madaio, who’s that? Why is Chuck Findley not there?” And I did the same with big band records because I’d look at the band and it’d be these set bands then all of a sudden it’d be somebody different in the personnel. “Well what happened to” such-and-such? Did they die? Did they get fired? You know, and I saw things like that as a kid. But I love looking at liner notes and reading who was on what. And then you’d start seeing the names crossing over, like maybe some of the big band things. And then you’d see Snooky Young’s name on a pop record in the horn © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
section. You’d go, “Wow, isn’t he with Count Basie? How could he be doing these two gigs at once?”
